facts.fact: The Adwave article states that email lists on average lose 22% to 30% of subscribers every year, through job changes, address switches, or lost interest; no source is named for this figure.
facts.quote: On average, you can expect to lose **22% to 30% of your subscribers every year** as people change jobs

facts.fact: The Adwave article says smart re-engagement tactics can raise email open rates from 14% to 45%, presented as the author's own experience.
facts.quote: smart re-engagement tactics can boost open rates from a dismal **14%** all the way up to **45%**

facts.fact: The Adwave article suggests treating a realtor sending weekly market reports as inactive after 90 days without engagement.
facts.quote: For a realtor sending weekly market reports, **90 days** of radio silence is a pretty clear signal.

facts.fact: The Adwave article suggests treating a local boutique sending daily deals as inactive after 30 days without engagement.
facts.quote: for a local boutique blasting out daily deals, you might want to consider someone inactive after just **30 days**.

facts.fact: The Adwave article gives an example of a win-back automation that triggers for any subscriber who has not opened or clicked an email in 60 days.
facts.quote: any subscriber who hasn't opened or clicked an email in the last **60 days** is automatically funneled into your re-engagement flow.

facts.fact: The Adwave article recommends a re-engagement sequence of three to five emails sent over about two weeks.
facts.quote: I've found a series of **three to five emails** sent over about two weeks is the sweet spot.

facts.fact: The Adwave article recommends splitting inactive subscribers into three segments: Once-Actives, Never-Actives, and Low-Engagement Users.
facts.quote: I recommend starting with three main buckets:

facts.fact: Adwave states that its TV ad campaigns can run for as little as $30 per day, with targeting limited to the viewer's service area.
facts.quote: campaigns can run for as little as **$30/day**, and target viewers right in your service area.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its commercial runs across dozens of top-tier streaming channels.
facts.quote: Your commercial runs across dozens of top-tier streaming channels.

facts.fact: Adwave claims its platform lets local businesses create and run polished TV ads in just a few minutes.
facts.quote: letting you create and run polished TV ads in just a few minutes.

facts.fact: Adwave states that most brands have 7 to 8 inactive subscribers for every active subscriber.
facts.quote: most brands have **7 to 8 inactive subscribers for every active one**

facts.fact: Adwave states that winning back about 5% of inactive subscribers can boost an engaged list by 35-40%, as an illustrative example.
facts.quote: Winning back even a tiny fraction, say **5%**, can boost your engaged list by **35-40%**.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a re-engagement sequence of three to five emails sent over 10 to 14 days.
facts.quote: Try a sequence of three to five re-engagement emails over 10 to 14 days.

facts.fact: Adwave says a solid re-engagement campaign can see success rates from 14% to 29%.
facts.quote: A solid re-engagement campaign can see success rates anywhere from **14% to 29%**.

facts.fact: Adwave reports a campaign that moved from a 14% average open rate to a 45% open rate.
facts.quote: We've seen campaigns jump from a dismal 14% average open rate to a stellar 45%

facts.fact: Adwave says re-engagement campaigns can lock in a 20% re-engagement on read rate.
facts.quote: and lock in a **20% re-engagement on read rates**

facts.fact: Adwave states that natural list churn removes 22.71% of an audience every year.
facts.quote: With natural list churn eating away at **22.71%** of your audience every year

facts.fact: Adwave advises removing subscribers who did not respond after a re-engagement campaign ends, rather than deleting them before running a campaign.
facts.quote: after the campaign ends, you absolutely **must** remove the people who didn’t respond.
